title: Where is the cat?
grammar: in, on, under, behind, next to, between

scene.speaker: valentina
scene.bubble: The neighbour's cat is somewhere in our club house — and Luna is NOT happy about it!
scene.intro: The neighbour's cat is somewhere in the club house — and Luna knows it! Is it under the table? No. Is it behind the door? No. Is it between the boxes, next to the window, in front of the shelf? Valentina looks everywhere. Finally Mateo looks up: the cat is ON the cupboard, watching everybody, very comfortable. Where are your things? Say it exactly!

activities.title: Match the preposition with the picture idea.

pairs.right: you can't see it from the front
in the middle of two things

activities.title: Quick check · Where is it? Choose the correct preposition.

The clock is ___ the door, up on the wall.
The bin is ___ the desk and the wall.
My bag is ___ the chair — you can't see it from here.
The keys are ___ the drawer, inside.

activities.title: Listen to the cat hunt. Write a word in each gap.

data.script: Valentina: Operation Find The Cat! Mateo, look under the sofa. … Mateo: Not under the sofa. Only three biscuits. Old ones. … Valentina: Behind the curtains? … Mateo: No… wait! White hairs ON the armchair. She was here! … Valentina: Check between the bookshelf and the window. … Mateo: There she is! Sleeping in Erik's toolbox! … Valentina: In the toolbox! And where is Luna? … Mateo: Hiding behind the door. I think the cat won this game.

data.text: Hide-and-tell: put your rubber somewhere (under the book, behind the case…). Your partner asks: "Is it under…? Is it behind…?" Maximum 6 questions. Then swap.

activities.title: A and B are not the same. Find out why!
activities.instructions: Look at picture A and picture B. Find the 12 differences and tell your partner about them.

homework.prompt: Write 6 sentences about where things are in your room, one for each preposition of activity A.

outcomes.puede: Understand short dialogues with more vocabulary; identify main information in simple announcements.
Describe routines, favourites, community helpers; give short opinions.
Read short paragraphs; answer simple comprehension Qs; find specific info.
Write short paragraph about self/family/routine (40–70 words).
~800 words; All basic tenses start; must/have to/could; SVA; superlatives.
